skill.name: convex-billing
skill.description: Add Stripe subscription billing to a Convex application with checkout, verified webhooks, stored subscription state, and server-side access checks.
skill.summary: Implement Stripe subscriptions in Convex with the @convex-dev/stripe component.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately invokes npm and npx to install dependencies and deploy Convex functions. Most static detections are Markdown or configuration references, but the checkout example trusts a client-supplied Stripe price identifier without server-side validation.

remediation.issue: The checkout action accepts any authenticated client-supplied price ID.
remediation.suggestion: Map approved plans to server-controlled Stripe price IDs and reject any value outside that allowlist before creating checkout sessions.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs npm and npx commands that execute package code and can update a Convex deployment.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before execution, review package provenance, use a lockfile, and verify the selected Convex deployment before pushing functions.

content.value_statement: Subscription billing requires coordinated checkout, webhook, and access-control logic. This skill provides a focused Convex workflow using the maintained Stripe component.
actual_capabilities: Configures the Stripe webhook route in Convex.
Creates an authenticated subscription checkout action.
Associates Stripe customers with authenticated Convex users.
Checks stored subscription status in a server-side query.
Lists required Stripe and Convex environment configuration.
limitations: The example requires an existing Convex application with authentication.
It covers subscriptions, not one-time payments, refunds, taxes, or invoices.
The sample accepts a client-provided price ID and requires an application-specific allowlist.
The access query returns a binary status and does not model plan-specific entitlements.

output_examples.input: Check whether my billing setup is ready for production.
output: Confirms webhook signing and protected secret storage.
Flags client-controlled price identifiers for server-side validation.

best_practices: Keep Stripe secrets in Convex environment storage and use separate test and production values.
Map plan names to approved Stripe price IDs on the server.
Gate paid features with server-stored subscription state instead of client claims.
anti_patterns: Do not trust arbitrary price IDs supplied by clients.
Do not implement webhook signature verification manually when the component already provides it.
Do not grant access from client-side payment state or checkout success parameters.

faq.question: Does this skill support Stripe subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates subscription checkout and checks active or trialing subscription state stored by the Convex component.

faq.question: Does it support one-time payments?
faq.answer: No. The provided workflow uses subscription mode and requires adaptation for one-time payment flows.

faq.question: Where should Stripe secrets be stored?
faq.answer: Store STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in Convex environment storage. Never place live values in source files.

faq.question: Does the webhook verify Stripe signatures?
faq.answer: Yes. The registered @convex-dev/stripe route handles signature verification when configured with the correct webhook secret.

faq.question: Can clients choose any Stripe price?
faq.answer: The sample permits this, but production code should map approved plans to price IDs on the server.

faq.question: How does the skill protect paid features?
faq.answer: It queries component-managed subscription records for the authenticated user. Applications should extend this check for plan-specific entitlements.
